paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the LORD deals with every destroyer, and He stays with His people. Isaiah opens with a woe on the one who destroys and betrays, and says, "When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed." (Isaiah 33:1) The nations scatter when the LORD rises, and He says, "Now I will arise." (Isaiah 33:3, 10) So no matter how big a bully gets, he doesn't get the last word.

Now look at what the people do while the trouble is going on. They pray, "O LORD, be gracious to us! We wait for You. Be our strength every morning and our salvation in time of trouble." (Isaiah 33:2) Notice that it says EVERY morning, not just the bad ones. Then comes the scary question from the sinners in Zion, "Who of us can dwell with a consuming fire?" (Isaiah 33:14) And the answer describes someone who walks righteously, speaks with sincerity, and won't take a bribe. (Isaiah 33:15)

And here's the good news that makes me want to run a lap around my bakery on my gold base. The LORD is the sure foundation, and "the fear of the LORD is Zion's treasure." (Isaiah 33:6) The passage ends with a King in His beauty, and with the promise that "the LORD is our Judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our King. It is He who will save us." (Isaiah 33:17, 22) The people who dwell there "will be forgiven of iniquity." (Isaiah 33:24) So wait on Him, baker, because He is the One who saves.
